messages:
Maya (Support): Heads-up — multiple customers reporting 503s from hosted inference since ~10:05 UTC. Customers see spike then steady 503s for ~2–3m. I'm attaching the chunk of logs we got from the gateway call.
Maya (Support): snippet: `2026-03-17T10:05:12Z infer-runner[pid=2345]: SIGSEGV at 0x7f...; GPU memory alloc failed, attempted 12.3G > avail 11.8G; container restart` 
Maya (Support): Customers impacted are on model: open-std-large v2026-03-01, QPS ~120 during incident window. No config changes from customer side.
Raj (Oncall): Looking. Can you paste `kubectl describe pod` and last 200 lines `kubectl logs --previous` from one of the failing pods?
Maya (Support): Got logs from one pod: ```kubectl logs infer-runner-7f9c -n hosted --previous --tail=200
2026-03-17T10:05:11Z runtime: cudaMemcpy failed: out of memory
2026-03-17T10:05:11Z inference: kv_prefetch triggered for key=ctx-1234 size=6.1G
2026-03-17T10:05:11Z infer-runner: fatal signal 11 (Segmentation fault)
``` 
Clara (eng-runtime): kv_prefetch + large batch = classic memory spike. Does the pod have strict cgroup mem.limit? Could be the OOM killer inside container or GPU oom leading to segfault.
Tom (eng-ml): Model changed? Any recent rollout of v2026-03-01 with different attention or prefetched keys? Prefetch can blow up if context distribution changes.
Maya (Support): No release noted in our release log for that model during that window.
Raj (Oncall): I've pulled node dmesg from the host: `Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (infer-runner) total-vm:10240000k, anon-rss:9800000k` — looks like host-level memory OOM, not just GPU. 
Clara (eng-runtime): Host OOM suggests process allocated huge CPU-memory during kv_prefetch. We should disable prefetch per-deployment as a short mitigation: set env `REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=0` for that deployment/class.
Tom (eng-ml): Also possible growth due to larger sequence lengths in incoming requests. Can we surface per-request seq length hist? If > 4096 tail, that'll increase RAM and KV sizes.
Maya (Support): Customer provided sample request: context size ~5200 tokens for a small fraction of requests.
Raj (Oncall): Action plan proposal:
- Immediately patch deployment with `REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=0` and smaller `BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=4096` (short-term mitigation)
- Add prebuilt fallback routing to smaller-ram variant (open-std-medium) for this customer
- Engineering to investigate memory accounting + cgroup limits vs host overcommit
Clara (eng-runtime): I can roll the env toggle to the hosted pool with a canary (5% traffic) in ~6m. Command I'll run:
```
kubectl set env deployment/infer-runner REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=0 -n hosted
kubectl rollout status deployment/infer-runner -n hosted --watch
```
Clara (eng-runtime): Also recommend increasing container memory limit for the pool from 12Gi -> 16Gi as a second short-term safety net.
Tom (eng-ml): For medium-term: add a hard cap on prefetch size and reject requests > 4096 tokens with 400 with guidance. We'll add an eval to measure how many requests would be blocked.
Maya (Support): I've notified the impacted customers and applied temporary routing to retry to the dedicated fallback where possible. They're asking for ETA.
Raj (Oncall): I'll start ramping the canary patch now. If we still see segfaults within canary, we'll rollback immediately and enable fallback routing cluster-wide.
SRE-bot: deploy-bot: Deployment infer-runner env update triggered by Clara. Canary 5% -> rollout started at 2026-03-17T10:12:00Z.
Clara (eng-runtime): Canary logs look good so far. No new SIGSEGV for canary pods in 6m.
Raj (Oncall): Rolling to 100% now. Monitor for 15m. If any host-level OOM messages appear, we pause.
Maya (Support): Customers reporting errors dropping. One customer says retries are succeeding now. :thumbsup:
Tom (eng-ml): We'll still track root cause: why kv_prefetch grew to 6G. Likely combination of longer contexts + prefetching policy not checking mem caps.
Clara (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: (1) instrument per-request KV size metric and add alert at 4G per-pod, (2) enforce prefetch cap in runtime code, (3) review pod memory limits for hosted pools and node sizing.
Raj (Oncall): Creating an incident ticket INC-2026-1842 and attaching logs. Assigning to @Clara and @Tom. 
Maya (Support): Adding customer impact notes + timeline to ticket. Thanks team.
Clara (eng-runtime): I'll push a code fix next week to limit prefetch and add soft-fail to avoid segfaults. For now mitigations done.
Maya (Support): Closing customer escalations contingent on 24h stability window. Will re-open if we see regressions.
